title: August .NET updates break printing and PDF export in WPF apps
originalTitle: Microsoft: August updates break printing, PDF export in WPF apps
summary: Hold or roll back the August .NET Framework updates on WPF endpoints that print or export PDFs, Microsoft acknowledged the issue and posted temporary mitigations.

title: Spring framework ships fixes for 91 flaws, update dependencies
originalTitle: 91 Vulnerabilities Patched in Spring Application Framework
summary: Upgrade Spring components to current versions and run regression tests, a large batch of vulnerabilities were patched this year raising exposure for Java apps common in SMB stacks.

title: Critical Keycloak bug allows unauthenticated account takeovers
originalTitle: Critical Keycloak Password Reset Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Take Over Any Account
summary: Update Keycloak to patched releases immediately, a 9.1 CVSS password reset flaw lets attackers trigger resets and seize any account including admins.

title: CISA’s logging blueprint works for SMBs too
originalTitle: CISA’s logging guidance works beyond government
summary: Borrow CISA’s new Logging Reference Architecture to prioritize actionable telemetry, align storage and retention, and ensure you can reconstruct incidents when it counts.

title: CISA: Patch actively exploited Zimbra bug within 3 days
originalTitle: CISA orders urgent patching of actively exploited Zimbra flaw
summary: Patch Zimbra Collaboration Suite now, actively exploited flaw added to KEV, federal agencies have 3 days, MSPs should expedite and monitor for compromise.

title: Criminal group uses AI to scale server attacks, deploys rootkit
originalTitle: UAT-10147 Uses AI to Scale Server Attacks, Deploys SPECTRE With EDR Bypass and Linux Rootkit
summary: Lock down internet-facing Windows and Linux servers, a Chinese-speaking crew is automating mass exploitation and dropping EDR-bypassing malware and a Linux rootkit.

title: Tool shows what your AI chats reveal
originalTitle: Product showcase: AI Paper Trail shows the privacy cost of talking to AI
summary: Audit exported AI chats to see what personal or sensitive data can be inferred, then set usage policies and remind staff that chat logs persist and can leak.

title: Cloaked fake bank sites evade scanners, steal credentials
originalTitle: Fake bank websites play dead to evade security scanners
summary: Watch for SEO poisoning and cloaked phishing pages, attackers are hiding fake banking sites from scanners and luring users via manipulated search results to steal credentials.

title: Ransomware crews target mid-market companies
originalTitle: Ransomware attackers are zeroing in on mid-market companies
summary: Mid-sized firms account for 73% of recent ransomware and data extortion incidents, tighten backups, MFA on remote access, vendor risk checks and response plans to reduce exposure.

title: AWS Network Firewall adds rule hit counts
originalTitle: AWS makes it easier to spot firewall rules that have gone quiet
summary: Use new rule hit counts to find unused or redundant stateful rules, validate control coverage and clean up AWS Network Firewall policies, note stateless rules are not covered.

title: ToxicPanda Android malware now blocks Google Play via VPN abuse
originalTitle: ToxicPanda Android malware uses VPN permissions to block Google Play
summary: Audit managed Android devices and block sideloading; ToxicPanda now targets 349 apps and abuses VPN permissions to disable Google Play protections while executing 167 remote commands.

title: Android car head units hijacked via malicious update app
originalTitle: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
summary: Lock down update channels and verify firmware signatures on Android head units—trojanized device-update apps are conscripting them into proxy botnets and ad fraud via a supply-chain attack.

title: Lock down Windows named pipes before attackers do
originalTitle: Named Pipes Under Attack: Securing Windows Interprocess Communication
summary: Review named pipe ACLs and service exposure on Windows endpoints—weak IPC lets untrusted processes poke privileged services; implement endpoint verification, command authorization, strict input validation, and least-privilege.

title: Banking trojans surge: Manic, Grandoreiro, ToxicPanda 2.0
originalTitle: Banking Trojans Manic, Grandoreiro, ToxicPanda 2.0 in the Spotlight
summary: Strengthen email filtering and browser protections—active banking trojans Manic, Grandoreiro, and ToxicPanda 2.0 target SMBs for credential theft; monitor banking sessions and enforce MFA.
